chunks: And a group informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyash, who said: Narrated to me Ibn Marwan al-Kufi, who said: Narrated to me Ibn Abi Sura, who said:

I was in al-Hayr visiting on the eve of Arafah. I set out heading along the land route. When I reached al-Musnath, I sat by it to rest, then got up and walked. A man was on the road and said to me: 'Do you want company?' I said: 'Yes.' We walked together, he narrated to me and I narrated to him, and he asked me about my condition. I informed him that I was in hardship, having nothing with me or in my hand. He turned to me and said to me: 'When you enter Kufa, go to the house of Abu Tahir al-Zarari and knock on his door. He will come out to you with the blood of sacrifice on his hand, and say to him: You are asked to give this man the purse of dinars that are with the man of the bedstead.' I was amazed by this. Then he parted from me and went his way, I do not know where he went. I entered Kufa and headed to the house of Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Zarari. I knocked on his door as he had told me, and he came out to me with the blood of sacrifice on his hand. I said to him: 'You are asked to give this man the purse of dinars that are with the man of the bedstead.' He said: 'Hearing and obeying,' and entered and brought out the purse to me and handed it to me. I took it and departed.

key_terms.أَبُو طَاهِرَ الزَّرَّارِي: Abu Tahir al-Zarari, a known companion
key_terms.الْمُسْنَاة: Al-Musnath, a place on the road

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Ibn Abi Sura and the purse of dinars in Kitab al-Ghayba?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the concept of *al-Kashf* (unveiling) during the Minor Occultation, where the Imam maintained direct economic and social ties with his followers through trusted agents like Abu Tahir al-Zarari. The specific detail of the Imam holding the blood of the sacrificial animal (*dam al-adahi*) while delivering the message underscores the continuity of religious authority and ritual practice even in his physical absence. This event serves as a key proof for the Shia belief in the Imam’s ongoing presence and ability to manage communal affairs from concealment. [ {
